svg.aria-label: Map of the Persian Gulf, the Arabian peninsula and the Red Sea. A wide grey lane shows the pre-war tanker route out of the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz; over it a red dotted line marks the direct route for large tankers as stopped, with strike markers in and just outside the strait. An amber dashed line shows small shuttle tankers running from Basra and Ras Tanura through the strait to a ship-to-ship transfer zone in the Gulf of Oman. A green line marks the Habshan to Fujairah pipeline in the UAE, which skips the strait. A thick amber line marks Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline across the peninsula to Yanbu on the Red Sea, with a strike marker where pumping stations were hit on 10 September. From Yanbu a green line runs north to Suez and Europe, and an amber line runs south through Bab el-Mandeb, where the Houthis took Mokha and Perim in September and Yemen's government claimed to have retaken Mokha on 5 October.
svg.text: How Gulf crude gets out now
the strait is shut to normal traffic; the oil leaves by pipeline, by shuttle tanker, and through a contested Red Sea
